Per file_changes, the changed hunks are head 872-878 (performance-measurement freshness ordering), 1123-1183 (TTFT admission estimator corrections, with the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 kill switch) and 2098. Those hunks fall outside the supplied head excerpts (lines 1-797) and appear only in the truncated patch excerpt. The visible text covers the Nemotron Super managed slot, load fit, prefix bank, MTP, media admission and the GLM5Next boundary. It is pre-existing prose, not a PR change.

No code or control change is visible. The patch text I can see describes out-of-order completed observations, rate freshness anchoring and estimator corrections. These touch availability and admission (T-010 and T-029 are adjacent), but they are only described, not implemented here.

The visible prose is consistent with the threat model. Prefix reuse is partitioned by authenticated cache scope and is off without one, which matches T-041. Media and image requests are reserved and bounded before decode. The slot emits no cache receipts.

Remaining questions for integration: if the corresponding source changes (EnginePerformanceMeasurements.Rate, AdmissionRateEstimators.swift) are in other batches, check that the freshness/expiry anchoring cannot let a provider inflate its own performance evidence. Also check that the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES kill switch does not weaken physical admission. I report no findings from the documentation alone.
